In real Hilbert H=L²(circle,C²), the parallelogram identity proves every minimizer of equal-weight orbit-distance squared lies at a midpoint of optimally shifted pair samples, so no hidden higher-harmonic minimizer exists. Cross correlation cosφ-a²cos2φ=a²+x-2a²x² is a strictly concave quadratic in x=cosφ, proving one mean for a<=1/2 and exactly two inequivalent means for a>1/2; variance and optimizer gap follow algebraically. At m0=(e^{it},0), each best phase shift is exactly zero; yet C_a''(0)=4a²-1>0 makes nearby midpoint classes strictly better when a>1/2, so algorithm fixed point is not even a local minimum.
